items.name: PrismML Bonsai 1-bit LLM (Snapdragon smart glasses)
items.summary: PrismML unveiled a 2B-parameter 1-bit version of its Bonsai LLM, showcased at Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit on Sept 24, that runs fully on-device on the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 Platform for real-time vision-language queries in smart glasses. It advances PrismML's open-weight, on-device AI vision as an alternative to cloud-dependent proprietary models — though no shipping glasses using it have been announced yet.

items.name: Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 on Sept 22 as the first model in the new 5.5 family, matching Claude Fable 5.1's performance while costing ~40% less to run ($4/$20 per Mtok) and generating output 30%+ faster. Aimed at enterprise agentic coding, computer use, and long-running knowledge work, it ships with strengthened safety guardrails and raised usage limits on paid plans.

items.name: Xiaomi MiMo V2.6 (Pro / Flash / Pro UltraSpeed)
items.summary: Xiaomi released the MiMo V2.6 family on Sept 21 under the MIT license, with the ~1T-parameter Pro topping Artificial Analysis's open-model rankings (score 46, tying Grok 4.7) while costing $0.435/$0.87 per Mtok — far cheaper than closed frontier models. Trained via ~750K RL trajectories in under six days for ~$2.62M, it marks the cheapest frontier-class open-weights release to date.

items.name: xAI Grok 4.7
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.7 on Sept 21, a larger base model with longer RL training aimed at coding, agentic workflows, and knowledge work, with a 500K-token context window and four reasoning-effort levels. It scores 46 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index (up from 44) with per-token pricing unchanged from Grok 4.6 ($2/$6 per Mtok).

items.name: xAI Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0
items.summary: xAI launched Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 on Sept 18, a speech-to-text model it claims is twice as accurate as v1.0, ranking first among 32 streaming models on Artificial Analysis's leaderboard. Batch pricing holds at $0.10/hour of audio with no code changes for existing integrations; v1.0 will be deprecated in the coming weeks.
